claims.text: The formation and persistence of a protective oxide scale in CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C is governed primarily by the intrinsic oxide-forming ability of X.
CrFeCoNiAl will form a continuous Al2O3 scale.
Al2O3 is a slow-growing and thermodynamically stable protective oxide at high temperature.
The alumina scale on CrFeCoNiAl will be adherent and resist cracking and spallation.
Oxides formed by the Mn- and Si-bearing variants have lower thermodynamic stability and adhesion than the alumina scale.
CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNiSi will form discontinuous or spalling oxide scales.
The studied alloys have nominal equiatomic CrFeCoNiX compositions.
All three nominal equiatomic CrFeCoNiX variants can be prepared as single-phase, homogeneous metallic solid solutions.
Identical processing can make the identity of X the only controlled variable among the Si-, Mn-, and Al-bearing alloys.
Exposure durations can be selected that are sufficient to develop equilibrium oxide scales between 900 and 1100 °C.
The nature, continuity, and coherence of the oxide scale mediate stress and determine adhesion at the metal/oxide interface.
Al's oxygen affinity promotes formation of a slow-growing, stable alumina scale.
Mn- and Si-derived oxides are more volatile or become discontinuous because of their oxidation kinetics and oxygen affinity.
Thermal stress will preferentially cause cracking or spallation of the Mn- and Si-bearing scales.
Under equivalent oxidation conditions, CrFeCoNiAl will have fewer cracked areas than CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn, whose scales will show more porosity, cracking, or spallation.
The proposed behavior applies only while the CrFeCoNiX alloys remain single-phase metallic solid solutions during exposure at or above 900 °C.
Minor phase separation, precipitation, and other microstructural variations can influence oxide-scale development.
Failure of CrFeCoNiAl to form continuous adherent alumina, or formation of comparably stable and adherent scales on the Si- or Mn-bearing alloys, would falsify the hypothesis.
